summary: This note is the Taylor and Francis Online article page for 'Friend or foe? The impact of macroprudential policy on economic growth' by Hiep Ngoc Luu, Thao Thi Phuong Nguyen, Tram Thi Mai Pham and Tram Ngoc Nguyen, published in the Journal of Economic Policy Reform (Volume 27, 2024, Issue 1). The paper finds that macroprudential policies generally foster economic growth, especially after the global financial crisis, but that excessive tightening can harm growth. Much of the page is site navigation, purchase options and related-article listings, which were ignored.
one_line: A 2024 study finding that macroprudential policy tightening generally boosts economic growth, but excessive tightening hurts it.
key_facts: The article 'Friend or foe? The impact of macroprudential policy on economic growth' was published in the Journal of Economic Policy Reform, Volume 27, 2024, Issue 1.
The authors are Hiep Ngoc Luu, Thao Thi Phuong Nguyen, Tram Thi Mai Pham and Tram Ngoc Nguyen.
The article was received on 09 Feb 2023, accepted on 06 Nov 2023, and published online on 29 Nov 2023.
The article appears on pages 87-106 and has DOI 10.1080/17487870.2023.2281646.
The study finds that implementing macroprudential policies contributes to fostering economic growth, especially in the period following the onset of the global financial crisis.

The study reports that tightening loan loss provisions, loan-to-value, lending restriction, liquidity requirements and systemically important financial institutions measures all lead to higher economic growth.
The study finds that excessive tightening of macroprudential policy can exert a negative growth impact, although tightening is generally beneficial.
The keywords are macroprudential policy, economic growth and two-step system GMM.
The JEL codes are E58, G28 and O4.
The research is funded by VNU University of Economics and Business under grant number BBQT.09.2022.
The authors re-estimated the baseline models using pooled OLS, random effects and fixed effects, with results in Appendix 2.
The authors excluded the seventeenth instrument (Other) from their analysis because it does not imply a specific nature and objective.
The article had 82 views and 0 CrossRef citations at the time the page was captured.
Mariana Mazzucato's article 'Governing the economics of the common good' appears among related research in the same journal.
